section_heading: Work while your course is in session
text: Student visa holders may work up to 48 hours in a fortnight while their course is in session. A fortnight is a 14-day period. Students undertaking a master's degree by research or a doctoral degree, and their family members, are exempt from this limit. A student's own grant conditions should be checked in VEVO because visa conditions can differ.

Home Affairs says work experience is generally counted toward the 48-hour fortnightly student work limit whether it is paid or unpaid. The exception is a work-experience unit that is a mandatory component of the course and included in the course's CRICOS registration. Work placement beyond that registered requirement counts toward the limit. Check the current visa condition and course documentation before relying on an exception.

The student visa work limit applies while the course is in session. A student should add hours across every job and any work experience that is not an exempt mandatory course component. Home Affairs directs visa holders to check their individual conditions in VEVO. This passage complements the official placement exception: the exception depends on the registered course requirement, not simply on a placement being described as an internship.

section_heading: National Minimum Wage and award rates
text: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week before tax for adults whose employment is not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. Many jobs are covered by an award, which can set a different minimum rate and penalty rates. Casual employees covered by the National Minimum Wage receive a 25% casual loading. Check the current Fair Work pay guide for the job and age.

International students have the same minimum workplace protections as other employees, regardless of migration status under the Migration Act. An employee should receive a pay slip within one day of being paid. The Fair Work Ombudsman can provide help about pay and workplace rights; its fact sheet says a worker can contact it for information even if they are concerned about visa conditions. For personal disputes, seek individual advice rather than relying on a chatbot.

If an employer pays less than the applicable award or agreement rate, first identify the instrument that covers the job and retain rosters, timesheets, messages and pay records. The Fair Work Ombudsman offers information and assistance, including its Infoline. A missing pay slip is not an acceptable practice: employees should receive one within a day of being paid. The correct rate depends on age, job classification, hours and applicable award, so do not assume one universal rate.

section_heading: Check work rights after course completion
text: A Student visa page describes work limits while a course is in session and says students can work unlimited hours when the course is not in session. It does not mean every student automatically has unrestricted work rights after course completion: the person's visa status and conditions matter. Check the visa grant notice and VEVO, and obtain migration advice for individual circumstances. A different visa may be needed for work after a student visa ceases.

section_heading: What OSHC is and how long it applies
text: Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) is health insurance for international students living and studying in Australia. It is a visa requirement for most Student visa subclass 500 holders and should cover the student's entire stay in Australia. Home Affairs notes that OSHC must cover at least the course length and any additional visa stay period granted. Check the policy dates against the visa grant and insurer documents; do not assume a basic policy pays every health cost.

For a non-emergency illness, Study Melbourne recommends starting with a general practitioner (GP), which is often more affordable than going directly to a hospital. If the student pays upfront for a covered service, keep the receipt and submit a claim through the insurer's app, email or website. The amount returned depends on the policy and service. Check the insurer's current provider network and benefits before booking treatment.

Basic OSHC does not include optical care such as glasses or dental services such as check-ups, fillings or dental surgery. A student may choose to buy additional private cover, often called Extras, but should confirm its waiting periods, limits and price with the insurer. A service being medically useful does not automatically mean it is covered. Check the policy wording and seek urgent clinical care when needed rather than delaying treatment because of uncertainty about a claim.

OSHC policies can leave gaps between the insurer benefit and a provider's fee, and some services may not be covered. Study Melbourne advises students to check their specific policy, save receipts for services paid upfront, and claim through the insurer's app, email or website. For a non-emergency concern, a GP is often a more affordable first contact than a hospital. The insurer, not a general chatbot, can confirm the exact benefit for a planned service.

Australia has Reciprocal Health Care Agreements with a limited set of countries. Eligibility and the medically necessary services covered depend on the agreement and the person's circumstances; a reciprocal arrangement is not equivalent to universal Medicare access. Check Services Australia's current country list and conditions. Do not infer eligibility from nationality alone, and confirm directly with Services Australia before making a treatment or insurance decision.

section_heading: OSHC remains a Student visa requirement
text: Most international students on a Student visa subclass 500 must hold OSHC for their stay. A Reciprocal Health Care Agreement may provide access to some medically necessary treatment for eligible visitors, but it does not by itself establish that a student satisfies the visa's OSHC requirement. Students should keep the OSHC policy active and verify any exception directly with Home Affairs and the insurer before changing cover.

If someone is experiencing a medical emergency or is at immediate risk in Victoria, call Triple Zero (000) or go to a hospital emergency department. Tell the operator whether police, fire or ambulance is needed and give the exact location if possible. Study Melbourne also describes 112 for situations where the phone has no service or is not connected to the network. Do not use an information chatbot in place of emergency services.

Ambulance transport can involve charges and is not automatically covered by Medicare. Study Melbourne says emergency ambulance services are typically covered by OSHC, but students should check their own policy to verify the level of cover. For a non-emergency health question, use an appropriate medical service rather than calling an ambulance. Costs and insurance benefits can depend on the circumstances and policy terms.

Tap on at the start of each trip. Tap off at the end on trains, buses that accept myki, and tram trips that begin and end in Zone 2. For a tram trip that starts and ends in Zone 1, tap on but do not tap off. Tap on again when changing transport modes. A green light or phone confirmation indicates the tap registered; failing to tap correctly can mean there is no valid ticket or a default fare applies.

The International Student Travel Pass is a separate discounted travel product, not a concession automatically granted to every international student. Study Melbourne describes eligibility for full-time international undergraduate students at participating education providers. The pass offers a discount on eligible travel products; details, participating providers and current prices should be checked on the live program page before purchase. A student who is not eligible may still need a full-fare myki.

section_heading: myki and concession entitlement are different questions
text: myki is the payment system used on most public transport in Victoria; owning or topping up a myki does not itself prove concession eligibility. Eligibility for student discounts depends on the specific concession or travel-pass program and its criteria. Check the current Transport Victoria or Study Melbourne rules and carry any required proof. Do not assume an international student card or university ID automatically qualifies for a concession fare.

section_heading: From Melbourne Airport to the city
text: Study Melbourne lists SkyBus as a frequent connection between Melbourne Airport and Southern Cross Station in the city centre. Other options include taxis, rideshare, public buses and shuttles. Journey time and fares vary, so check the airport or operator's live timetable and price before travelling. The page also notes that Avalon Airport is a different airport with different transfer options; confirm which airport is on the ticket.

section_heading: What happens after travelling without a valid ticket
text: A passenger must hold and use a valid ticket for the trip. If a myki is not tapped correctly, Transport Victoria says it may not be a valid ticket and a passenger may be fined. An authorised officer may report an alleged offence; the Department of Transport and Planning decides whether to issue a warning, infringement or take another action. Current fine amounts and review options should be checked on the official page, not inferred from an old example.

section_heading: Where a Victorian rental bond is held
text: The Residential Tenancies Bond Authority (RTBA) holds Victorian residential rental bonds in trust. When a renter pays the bond to a rental provider, the provider must lodge it with the RTBA within 14 days. The renter should review and accept the online lodgement, check that the names and amount are correct, and keep the bond receipt and number. A bond is not the same as rent paid in advance.

A renter whose name is on a Victorian bond can start a bond claim through the RTBA after the rental agreement ends and must authenticate identity through Service Victoria. If the renter starts a claim, the other parties receive notice and have 14 days to contest it through the relevant dispute process. If all parties agree to a provider-started claim, the RTBA usually repays within one business day after everyone accepts. A disputed claim may require VCAT or RDRV.

section_heading: Bond repayment follows agreement or an order
text: At the end of a tenancy, the RTBA repays the bond as agreed by the renter and rental provider or as directed by VCAT or a court. The RTBA does not decide a disputed deduction merely because a landlord requests it. Renters should check the claim, keep evidence of property condition and payments, and use the official dispute pathway if the proposed allocation is not agreed. Current claim steps are managed online.

Before signing a Victorian rental agreement, read and keep a copy of the agreement and ask questions about unclear terms. At the start of the tenancy, the rental provider must give the renter a condition report and information including the provider or agent's contact details and an emergency contact number. Record the property's condition, return the report by the stated deadline and keep a copy with dated photographs. Check the current Consumer Affairs Victoria guidance for exact obligations.

section_heading: Urgent repairs in a rental property
text: Victorian urgent repairs include a blocked or broken toilet, gas leak, dangerous electrical fault, serious roof leak, or failure of an essential hot-water, water, cooking, heating or laundering service. Contact the rental provider or agent immediately using the emergency number provided at move-in and confirm the request in writing. The provider must arrange urgent repairs immediately. Keep records of contact attempts and receipts; continue paying rent while the repair is unresolved.

section_heading: If an urgent repair is not arranged
text: If the provider or agent does not respond promptly after being notified, a renter may organise and pay for an urgent repair costing $2,500 or less, then send written notice and receipts requesting repayment. The provider has seven days after receiving the notice to repay. For a repair over $2,500, do not arrange it yourself under this pathway; apply to Rental Dispute Resolution Victoria (RDRV) for help. The official page was last updated 26 February 2026.

Rent in advance is rent paid before the period it covers; it is a payment to the rental provider and is not money held as a bond. Victorian rules limit how much rent can usually be requested in advance, with exceptions such as rent above the statutory weekly threshold. The precise limit depends on the payment frequency and rent amount. Check the current Consumer Affairs Victoria page and keep a receipt showing which rental period the payment covers.

Study Melbourne describes private rentals, student accommodation, homestay and short-term stays as possible housing options. Availability, contract terms and costs differ. Students are advised to inspect accommodation before signing or paying where possible, read the agreement, understand what is included, and use official or reputable provider information. A homestay arrangement is not necessarily the same legal arrangement as a residential tenancy, so check the agreement and obtain advice if the terms are unclear.

Banks set their own identity and application requirements. Study Melbourne recommends checking the selected bank's current document list; students commonly need identity evidence such as a passport and may be asked for enrolment or address information. Some banks let a new arrival start the process before travelling, but identity verification may still be required in Australia. Compare fees and access arrangements, and never send identity documents through an unverified link.

section_heading: Applying for a tax file number
text: A tax file number (TFN) is a personal identifier used in the Australian tax and superannuation system. Eligible foreign passport holders and temporary visitors can apply online through the Australian Taxation Office's foreign-passport-holder process while in Australia, using the identity documents listed by the ATO. Applying for a TFN is free. Use the official ATO service rather than a paid intermediary, and do not share the TFN publicly because it is sensitive personal information.

An overseas student enrolled in an Australian course lasting six months or more may be an Australian resident for tax purposes, but this is not automatic solely because of a visa. Tax residency is assessed under the relevant tests and facts. If resident, a person generally reports income according to ATO rules, which may differ for temporary residents and foreign income. Use the ATO residency tool or a registered tax professional for a personal determination.

section_heading: Whether a tax return must be lodged
text: Whether a person must lodge a tax return depends on their income, residency, withholding and other circumstances for that financial year. The ATO provides a current 'Do I need to lodge a tax return?' tool; use the tool for the relevant year rather than relying on a general student rule. If a return is not required, the ATO may still require a non-lodgment advice. Keep income statements and seek registered tax advice for complex cases.

section_heading: Declaring food at the Australian border
text: Travellers bringing food into Australia should read the current Australian Border Force and biosecurity rules before packing. Many food items must be declared on the Incoming Passenger Card, even if they may ultimately be allowed. Biosecurity officers may need to inspect some of the declared food. Do not assume commercially packaged, dried or familiar food is automatically permitted. Check the item-specific official guidance and declare when required.

Study Melbourne's pre-departure checklist recommends confirming travel and enrolment arrangements, keeping key documents accessible, knowing how to contact the education provider, and preparing health cover and money arrangements. It also recommends confirming accommodation for arrival, transport from the airport and telling the education provider the travel dates. This is a planning checklist rather than a legal rule; provider deadlines and current travel requirements can change.

section_heading: Applying for a Victorian Proof of Age card
text: A person without an Australian driver licence may apply for a Victorian Proof of Age card if they meet the age and identity requirements. Service Victoria lists original identity documents, a photograph and an authorised witness among the application requirements. The application has a fee and processing time that can change, so check the current application page before attending or submitting documents. A Proof of Age card is an identity document, not a visa or work-rights document.

section_heading: Other identity documents and proof of age
text: Study Melbourne explains that overseas students may use different identity documents in different settings. An overseas driver licence may need an English translation, and accepted proof-of-age documents depend on the organisation requesting them. A Proof of Age card is one Victorian option for a person who does not hold an Australian driver licence. Check the receiving organisation's rules before applying; the card does not replace a passport or establish immigration status.

Australian education providers commonly offer support such as academic skills assistance, counselling, accessibility support, international student advice and student wellbeing services. The services and eligibility vary by provider. Start with the university's international student or student support website, check opening hours and appointment requirements, and use emergency services for immediate danger. This general guide cannot confirm a particular student's entitlement or replace the provider's current policy.

Condition 8202 requires a Student visa holder to remain enrolled in a registered course, maintain the required Australian Qualifications Framework level, and maintain satisfactory attendance and course progress as required by the education provider. A registered course is listed on CRICOS. The provider sets the applicable study-period expectations. Students concerned about attendance, progress or changing courses should contact the provider promptly and check their visa grant conditions; individual migration advice may be needed.

Call Triple Zero (000) if there is an emergency, immediate danger or a crime happening now. When answered, say whether police, fire or ambulance is needed, explain the exact location and follow the operator's instructions. Study Melbourne notes 112 may be dialled when outside mobile coverage or not connected to the network, and 106 is for people with a speech or hearing impairment. Do not delay an emergency call to search online.

section_heading: Free legal help for international students
text: Study Melbourne's support hub can refer international students to free, confidential and independent legal advice about employment and accommodation concerns. The service is intended to help students understand options; availability and eligibility should be confirmed with the hub. For urgent danger call emergency services. A general chatbot cannot assess a legal case, advise whether to sign a specific contract, or guarantee an outcome. Keep relevant agreements, messages and receipts when seeking professional help.

section_heading: Finding the right student support contact
text: Students can also contact their education provider's international student office, student union or wellbeing service for referrals and practical support. These services are not substitutes for a lawyer and may not provide legal representation. Study Australia's student-support guidance is a starting point; check the current provider contacts and any confidentiality or eligibility information before sharing sensitive circumstances. If a student faces an immediate threat, use the relevant emergency service rather than waiting for an appointment.
